articles.title_orig: PHOTOS: Xi greets Trump as he arrives in China for APEC Summit
articles.title_zh: PHOTOS: Xi greets Trump as he arrives in China for APEC Summit
articles.content_orig:
Trump will participate this week in a trilateral meeting with Putin and Xi.
President Donald Trump is traveling to Asia for meetings with global leaders and for his second visit to China for a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping.
See the most recent developments below.
President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin greeted each other with a handshake on Wednesday as Chinese President Xi Jinping looked on.
The greeting came as a wider group of APEC leaders gathered for a group photo before a welcome banquet. The American, Chinese and Russian leaders are scheduled to hold a meeting on Thursday.
Putin on Wednesday said he sees "substantial potential benefit" in gatherings such as the APEC summit and the trilateral , which will take place on the gathering's sidelines.
Putin said such meetings allow for leaders to "sit at the same table, exchange views, resolve differences between states -- whether political, economic or security-related -- by seeking compromise and balancing interests," according to the text of his remarks published by his office.
Xi earlier said he looked forward to an exchange of views with Trump on major issues, including China-U.S. relations and Asia-Pacific cooperation, according to China's Xinhua News Agency.
-ABC News’ Joe Simonetti and Kevin Shalvey
In a surprise move, President Donald Trump was personally greeted by Chinese President Xi Jinping at the foot of Air Force One on Wednesday after the American president arrived in Shenzhen, China.
The Chinese president rolled out the red carpet and displayed pomp and circumstance complete with troops marching and dozens of enthusiastic dancers.
Xi emerged from his vehicle and walked down the red carpet to meet Trump at the bottom of the stairs, a shocking appearance from the Chinese president that was not expected. Xi did not greet Trump personally at the airport back in May when the president visited Beijing.
The move comes after Trump himself broke from protocol and greeted Xi on the tarmac at Joint Base Andrews during Xi's state visit to Washington in September.
Trump fist-pumped upon emerging from the Qatar-gifted Air Force One as a crowd in pink and blue outfits holding poms-poms chanted "warm welcome" in Mandarin, according to a pool reporter on the ground.
According to the pool, the arrival ceremony participants also included Chinese first lady Peng Liyuan, U.S. Ambassador to China David Perdue and his wife, Consul General Pauline Kao, along with China’s Executive Vice Minister of Foreign Affairs H.E. MA Zhaoxu and Ambassador of the People’s Republic of China to the United States H.E. XIE Feng.
The leaders stood side-by-side as the American national anthem played, with Trump standing at a salute for the song. After the Chinese anthem was played, there was a military flyover of five jets, which left plumes of red, blue and yellow, according to the pool reporter traveling with the president. Trump and Xi then made their way down the red carpet, before Trump entered his motorcade.
After 24 hours in Manila, Philippines, Trump landed in Shenzhen for the APEC summit, which starts on Wednesday, and his high-stakes meetings with Xi and Russia’s Vladimir Putin, which is scheduled for Thursday.
-ABC N ews' Michelle Stoddart, Emily Cha n g a n d Fritz Farrow
President Donald Trump announced a new trade agreement between the U.S. and the Philippines in Manila on Wednesday, describing it only as a "very big trade deal" without elaborating on the details of the agreement.
The White House did not immediately respond to a request for additional information. Trump indicated that the agreement was unexpected.
"We've just consummated a very big trade deal, the biggest trade deal we've ever made, by far, And it's a fair deal for both countries, and we're very happy with that," Trump said during the luncheon following a bilateral meeting with Filipino President Ferdinand Marcos.
"And we didn't know that that was going to take place, but it took place very quickly. And it's a magnificent deal for both," Trump said.
-ABC News' Nicholas Kerr, Michelle Stoddart, Fritz Farrow and Meghan Mistry
President Trump arrived at the palace of Philippine President Marcos for a bilateral meeting. Marcos warmly welcomed Trump, but also repeatedly noted how short Trump's visit to the summit is.
"The United States is our only treaty ally, and our relationship has continued to grow and evolve over the many years," Marcos said. "Now we are also exploring new areas of cooperation, particularly in technology, where American leadership and innovation continues to lead the way."
Marcos pointed specifically to artificial intelligence as one of the ways that the Philippines can work more closely with the U.S.
Trump was flanked by some of his top aides, including newly-tapped Chief of Staff Stephen Miller, Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.
The president pointed to a few key areas of cooperation, including energy and touted U.S. defense support for the Philippines that the leaders would build on during the visit.
"The United States is now the world's leading producer of oil and natural gas by a lot, and we've just announced a major new pipeline in Alaska to export affordable, abundant supplies of energy to our allies and friends across the Pacific. And the Philippines would be a very natural partner in this effort. We're working on that," Trump said.
Trump, who has long focused on his own renovation projects on the White House, praised the Philippine president's residence.
"We've been there together for a long time. Our people share common history, common values, common interests, common architectural tastes. I love what you've done here. You've done a fantastic job,” Trump said.

articles.title_orig: China seeks advanced Nvidia chips for AI weapons despite US curbs, report says
articles.title_zh: China seeks advanced Nvidia chips for AI weapons despite US curbs, report says
articles.content_orig:
China 's People's Liberation Army has been "actively soliciting" Nvidia 's most advanced semiconductor chips to develop its artificial intelligence-enabled military capabilities, a congressional commission said in a report released Wednesday.
The report comes as Nvidia has been rocked by the resignation of its CEO, Jensen Huang , after reports that he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy who worked for Singapore-based Megaspeed , which is being eyed by U.S. investigators for potential diversion of Nvidia's chips to China.
"China is seeking to evade U.S. export controls to gain the most advanced semiconductors that underpin its intelligentization drive," the U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission said in its 2026 annual report to Congress.
China is making that move as it faces a quality gap between chips produced by Chinese companies, including Huawei and Cambricon , and the more advanced ones produced by Nvidia and other U.S. companies, such as Advanced Micro Devices , the report noted.
The report's findings could fuel concerns about advanced Nvidia chips having found their way to Chinese users amid escalating investigations from Congress and state and federal regulators.
"Although China has made some progress in achieving its goals, it has not yet closed the hardest chokepoints — including the most advanced capabilities in logic fabrication, memory, and semiconductor manufacturing equipment, as well as the Nvidia Compute Unified Device Architecture (CUDA) software moat — and likely will not for some time," the report said.
"The resulting gap in compute is substantial, largely due to U.S. export controls on advanced chips," the report said.
The report highlighted the fact that in the meantime, Chinese companies have obtained remote access to Nvidia chips through data centers in third countries, including Malaysia.
On Tuesday, the Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security issued a rule intended to cut off that workaround.
The move came in response to criticism from Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Congress members that the Commerce Department had not done enough to prevent Nvidia's most advanced chips from being diverted to China in violation of U.S. export controls.
The U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission was created by Congress in 2000 with a mandate to monitor and report to Congress the national security implications of the trade and economic relationship between the U.S. and China.

articles.title_orig: In Choosing Shenzhen for Trump-Putin Summit, Xi Shows Off His Tech Ambitions
articles.title_zh: In Choosing Shenzhen for Trump-Putin Summit, Xi Shows Off His Tech Ambitions
articles.content_orig:
Host city offers showcase of China’s rise into a confident and innovative power central to global economy
I n a Shenzhen square on a balmy evening, locals and tourists watched the dozens of glinting towers that make up the city’s skyline ripple through the colour spectrum – cyan and violet, cyber green, China’s national scarlet and gold – repeatedly flashing the words “Apec 2026”.
The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit is a dream showcase for one of China’s most advanced cities, and the country’s leader, Xi Jinping , is basking in its neon glow.
On the sidelines, a series of high-profile bilateral meetings and the announcement of a historic three-way summit with Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin have cemented Xi’s status as an agenda setter on the global stage.
The broader Apec summit , meanwhile, provides an opportunity for China to present itself as a steward of multilateralism against what it terms “unilateralism and protectionism” – that is to say, trade measures taken against Beijing by countries such as the US.
All this is set against the futuristic backdrop that is Shenzhen, a city that perhaps better than no other embodies China’s rise into a confident, technologically innovative power central to the global economy.
A photo display in the Apec media centre charts Shenzhen’s transformation from sparsely populated marshland, calling it “a miracle in the history of world development created by the Chinese people”.
“[Xi] wants people to go home Chinamaxxing,” said Prof Astrid Nordin, of King’s College London. “Shenzhen is itself part of the message. It’s a showcase of Chinese technological and economic achievements, and of China’s claim that it offers opportunities for prosperity in a world increasingly characterised by uncertainty and conflict.”
Like the light show, the summit is being carefully coordinated. The Financial Times cited people familiar with the matter as saying it would be one of the most tightly controlled in the organisation’s history, with leaders having to travel to a state guesthouse beside Shenzhen’s tiger safari park to meet Xi. The paper said diplomats had grumbled that the format “seems designed to reduce the free-flowing discussion characteristic of prior editions”.
Setting out its expectations for the summit, China’s foreign ministry has said it looks forward to “practical results in key areas such as trade, connectivity, digital economy, AI and so on”.
Already, Xi has announced trade wins with Canada’s Mark Carney, extending remission measures for certain Chinese steel and aluminium products by two years in exchange for tariff relief on Canadian pork, fish and seafood exports.
A meeting with Papua New ⁠Guinea’s leader, meanwhile, showed how Beijing’s geopolitical priorities have been absorbed and reflected by its allies, with James Marape recounting to Xi how he had closed Taiwan’s office in his country despite domestic challenges in doing so.
The most important meeting will be between Xi and Trump. The leaders of the world’s two superpowers are expected to tackle a broad range of issues including AI and trade. In a move that could strain the fragile tariff truce that the two leaders first agreed last year, the Trump administration said on Monday it would further restrict China’s access to advanced AI chips.
Christopher Adams, a senior adviser at the law firm Covington who was at the centre of trade negotiations with China for the Obama and first Trump administrations, said: “The trade truce may increasingly look like a ceasefire in a war where major combat operations remain on hold but skirmishes are escalating to the point where the line between peace and war is blurred.
“I don’t see pressure to announce a further extension of the trade truce in Shenzhen. If a significant extension is announced, that would be an upside surprise.”
China has not hesitated to leverage Apec’s multinational platform in service of its arguments. A commentary by the state news agency Xinhua on Tuesday said: “Amid deepening geopolitical rivalries and growing global divisions, [China’s hosting] sends a clear signal that great-power competition need not be a zero-sum game, and that one country’s development need not come at the expense of another.”
The chair of the Apec senior officials’ meeting, Chen Xu, said Beijing had made trade “openness” a key focus of its Apec year and looked forward to “achieving more practical outcomes on the trade front”.
The much anticipated trilateral summit with Trump and Putin, on the other hand, could prove largely symbolic. For Xi, “it provides the appearance of China shaping the world order as an equal to the United States,” said Dr Kevork Oskanian, an expert on Russia at the University of Exeter. “Agreement on substantial issues, which would, in any case, require extensive preparatory negotiations, is unlikely.”
For China’s ruling Communist party, the political pomp has another key purpose. Nordin said summits were “occasions for leaders to tell stories about the world, about their country’s place in it … and one of the most important audiences for those stories is at home.”
For the locals watching the skyscraper light show on Monday night, the symbolism was not lost. China’s export might had helped it become increasingly powerful on the world stage, said one local man, who did not give his name. “It’s so great that the summit will take place in Shenzhen,” he said. “I feel very proud.”

articles.title_orig: Oxford protest against talk by academic who made Arday plagiarism claim
articles.title_zh: Oxford protest against talk by academic who made Arday plagiarism claim
articles.content_orig:
Hundreds of people gathered to protest against a talk at an Oxford University college by the academic who accused the late Professor Jason Arday of plagiarism.
Stand Up To Racism organised a demonstration against Nathan Cofnas's talk at Oriel College, organised by Oxford Reform UK, on Tuesday evening.
Protesters, some with face masks on, appeared to try to block the entrance gates to stop people getting into the college before the talk.
Dozens of protesters held signs saying "Nathan Cofnas not welcome" and "Remember Professor Jason Arday". Cofnas has been contacted for a comment.
Chants of "Nathan Cofnas shut him down" could be heard.
Cofnas, who has advocated for "race realism", wrote a blog accusing Prof Arday of plagiarism in his doctoral thesis.
It prompted a weeks-long plagiarism row that saw 41-year-old Arday face intense public scrutiny about his work and other achievements.
Although he denied the allegations made against him, Arday resigned his post as a Cambridge professor of sociology of education. He was found dead at his home in south London on 14 August.
Theo Biggs, 20, who is a student at nearby Oxford Brookes University, said: "Oxford University is a prestigious university, and what is talked about here is talked about around the world.
"Giving this sort of conversation a platform is legitimising it essentially."
A course administrator at the university, who did not want to be named, said: "I've seen a lot of students of colour are feeling unwelcome, uncomfortable, frightened by the fact that Oriel and the wider university has not shut this down."
Another student added: "I've worked really hard to get here. I pay a lot of money to be here, and then me being a minority is like the biggest sin in the world. It's not something I want, it's not something I'm standing for at all."
On its website, Oxford Reform UK writes the society was "dedicated to providing a space for free speech, serious discussion, and association between students, linked with ReformUK".
The talk's event page stated Cofnas "faced recent controversy after exposing the plagiarism of Jason Arday".
Cofnas has previously written that black people are less intelligent than other groups and would "disappear from almost all high-profile positions outside of sports and entertainment" under a meritocratic system.
He was suspended from Ghent University in Belgium in August before being reinstated after pressure by US ambassador Bill White.
On Thursday, protesters against the talk placed a Ku Klux Klan hood on a controversial statue of the 19th Century colonialist Cecil Rhodes at Oriel College.
In response to the protest, the college said it was "committed to upholding freedom of speech within the law and has a statutory duty to do so".
"We are also committed to promoting inclusion and maintaining an environment that is free from all forms of discrimination and harassment, including racial discrimination," it said.
It added that permitting the event "does not imply endorsement by the college of the views of its speakers".

articles.title_orig: Iran widens Gulf attacks, targeting US air base in Kuwait and sites in Bahrain
articles.title_zh: Iran widens Gulf attacks, targeting US air base in Kuwait and sites in Bahrain
articles.content_orig:
Iran said its army targeted U.S. drone and missile installations at Kuwait's Ali Al Salem air base, according to local media , extending a series of attacks on Gulf states hosting American forces.
Kuwait's army said on Tuesday evening that its air defenses had countered hostile drone attacks, without providing further details.
Tensions between Iran and the U.S. have escalated sharply in recent days as strikes resumed across the Middle East, even as diplomatic talks continued.
Bahrain has also sustained a wave of Iranian drone strikes , issuing an "all-clear" alert on Wednesday after its air defenses intercepted several aerial threats. Iran has previously claimed attacks on U.S. radar systems in Bahrain.
CNN reported late Monday that U.S. intelligence found Iran was developing plans that could involve a so-called dirty bomb to target Washington, D.C. The administration officials, including President Donald Trump, have played down any imminent threat while saying the government continues to monitor the situation.
Speaking at the Association of Southeast Asian Nations summit in Manila, Philippines, Trump warned that Iran would "pay a price the likes of which no country has ever paid before" if such a plan existed.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio echoed Trump's comments when addressing reporters in Manila, saying he did not see any imminent threats to the U.S. capital, but that the government is "always on the lookout for anything that's a threat."
Trump nodded and said, "We are looking into it," while adding, "We are doing very well in Iran."
The renewed attacks come as diplomatic efforts to end the U.S.-Israel war with Iran, now in its ninth month, appear to be stalled, while disruptions continue to weigh on energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz.
Crude futures settled lower amid signs of recovering oil flows through the critical waterway. The International Energy Agency said Friday that the global oil supply had surpassed demand for the first time since the outbreak of the war and projected the market will return to a surplus in the fourth quarter.
The U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures dropped 1.2% to $84.9 a barrel, while Brent was down 0.48% at $92.7 per barrel.

articles.title_zh: ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ is a cultural and economic earthquake. Brace yourself.
articles.content_orig:
Nov 12, 2026 [[read-time]] minute read
Grand Theft Auto VI officially launches on November 19th and the community on YouTube couldn’t be more hyped. To date, the Grand Theft Auto series has reached over 900 billion views on YouTube, with pre-launch videos related to GTAVI already topping 40 billion views. 1
To date, the Grand Theft Auto series has reached over 900 billion views on YouTube.
In celebration of GTAVI’s imminent launch, YouTube and Rockstar Games are partnering to bring the community together with Creator content and interactive features.
Here's how fans can take part in the action:
Eligible viewers tuning into select creator live streams can claim and send a Grand Theft Auto VI gift on us while they last.
YouTube Live is introducing five limited-edition, game-themed gifts , including iconic animations like Wanted Stars that pop up directly on screen during streams. To kick things off, eligible viewers tuning into select creator live streams can claim and send a Grand Theft Auto VI gift on us while they last.
Fans can drop themselves directly into Vice City using the GTAVI: Visit Vice City Shorts Effect. The feature includes multiple iconic backgrounds, making it easy for creators and fans to build their own launch-week videos.
Our global creators are bringing you everything from deep tactical breakdowns and immersive storytelling to behind-the-scenes access throughout launch week in Miami. Stay tuned to watch your favorite creators dive into Vice City!
Music has always been a defining part of the Grand Theft Auto experience. Listeners can find the official GTAVI soundtrack (featuring Morgan Wallen’s “Last Thing You Need”) and the complete GTA series anthology playlist directly on the YouTube Music homepage throughout launch week.
YouTube’s Culture & Trends team published an in-depth look at Grand Theft Auto's lasting cultural impact as we inch closer to the GTAVI era.
Today, YouTube’s Culture & Trends team published an in-depth look at Grand Theft Auto's lasting cultural impact as we inch closer to the GTAVI era. The report analyzes how the uniquely cinematic and immersive world has evolved digital storytelling and opened new avenues for creative expression. Read the full report here.
Starting November 19 at 12 AM ET, fans worldwide can tune in to youtube.com/youtube for a 24 hour stream packed with live gameplay, creator podcasts, and original content featuring top creators like Caylus , Zhong and Kat , Jelly , Rivers , Jake Baldino , Cinna and more! The marathon will kick off with a pre-show hosted by RDCWorld starting at 11 PM ET on November 18th and will wrap with live on-the-ground coverage from Miami, bringing viewers to the action alongside creators and special guests.
Fans can jump straight into the global broadcast by clicking the custom GTAVI -themed YouTube logo (Yoodle) on the YouTube homepage. 2
As launch approaches, YouTube is excited to be the place where the community experiences GTAVI together in real time.

articles.title_orig: Grand Theft Auto VI Uses AMD FSR 4 On Xbox Series S, Upscaling 720p To 1080p While Still Running Ray Traced Global Illumination
articles.title_zh: Grand Theft Auto VI Uses AMD FSR 4 On Xbox Series S, Upscaling 720p To 1080p While Still Running Ray Traced Global Illumination
articles.content_orig:
During Grand Theft Auto VI 's review period , Rockstar Games offered us the chance to send some questions to the developers. Being a tech-focused website, there was a lot we wanted to know about the studio's design goals for this iteration of the RAGE engine .
Did they try to achieve a frame rate higher than 30 frames per second ? What were the rendering resolutions for each system? What kind of challenges did adding ray traced global illumination present, and what was their approach to HDR support?
All of these questions are answered below in a lengthy statement crafted by Jonathon Ashcroft - Senior Vice President of Technology, Chris Oat – Technical Director: Engine and Graphics, and Marc Chambers – Technology Production Director.
It became clear early on that given the scale of the team’s ambition, we’d be targeting 30fps on this generation of hardware. We’ve put a lot of effort into balancing presentation, simulation, and gameplay, as well as ensuring the input latency is vastly improved vs. Grand Theft Auto V and Red Dead Redemption 2. Part of that process was determining our base resolution and upscaling solution. We evaluated a variety of approaches for each console, then selected a combination of each that gave us the look and performance we needed.
On all platforms, the picture is then composited with a 4K UI and presented. For each console, we’ve arrived at our solution through careful evaluation of both the visuals and the performance.  We built our core lighting, frame processing, and final presentation pipeline with both HDR and SDR support in mind from the outset. We calibrated our engine’s in-game light sources according to the real-world physical properties of natural and artificial light sources.
We also built a new physically-based material library used to represent every material type you will see in game. From the way muddy alligator skin glistens in the Leonida sunshine, to the way hair and clothing reacts to the dynamic light shows in a nightclub, and the complex lighting interactions of exotic vehicle paint zipping under highway street lights — it was all built to behave according the physical laws of light. Finally, that rendered frame goes through an imaging pipeline modelled after real word cinematic camera and film treatment, much like you would expect of a modern movie. The aim is always to try and create and preserve emersion for the player, so they can experience it as the team imagined it, whether they are experiencing the game in HDR or SDR.
This focus on lighting made it vital for us to ensure we could use the same lighting solution on each console, including the Xbox Series S, where memory pressure posed a bit of a challenge. The results made that a challenge worth overcoming. There are indeed some differences between the implementations per console, as we rebalance the RTGI features to achieve the best presentation based on each platform’s capabilities. As with everything, we tune on a given piece of hardware to achieve the presentation we’re looking for, so there’s no single solution.
I also asked Rockstar a couple of more artistic questions, which were answered separately by the studio's VP of Art, Michael Kane . You can find them below.
The game's corners of the screen often seem a little darkened, kind of like a vignette effect. Can you confirm that's the case? If so, would it be possible to add it as a toggle option for those who dislike it?
Michael Kane, Vice President of Art: Dynamic: The vignette effect is an artistic choice. We currently do not support any toggle, but we have recently identified and fixed an issue where it was becoming stronger than intended in certain circumstances.
In key Grand Theft Auto VI artworks, Jason looks very different from the in-game character, whereas Lucia looks much closer. How did your design for each character evolve through development, and did you have any specific references or inspirations that you can share?
Michael Kane, Vice President of Art: Dynamic: There could typically be a perceptual interpretation of the key art versus in-game, especially for Jason… because both of them are so customizable, we think many players will maybe want ‘their Jason’ to have a mustache or long hair in a certain style or colour etc when they play. So far, we’ve only seen those more diverse looks on him in screenshots and not key marketing art, so that’s the best anchor point for our intention for him – that’s his ground truth, in-game.
About the author : With over two decades of experience in gaming journalism, Alessio Palumbo has led the gaming vertical at Wccftech since August 2015. He started working at a young age for Italian websites like Everyeye.it, Gamestar.it, Nextgame.it, and Multiplayer.it before kickstarting the indie English-language publication Worlds Factory as its founder and Editor in Chief. 

In the last decade, he has coordinated the overall output of Wccftech's gaming section, managed PR relations, assigned reviews, produced daily news coverage, edited gaming content as needed, and delivered game reviews.  

Arguably, his trademark content is the long series of exclusive developer interviews that have been cited by Wikipedia and by the biggest news media and gaming publications. 

His passion for technology also makes him knowledgeable when it comes to gaming hardware and tech. His favorite genres include RPGs, MMORPGs, and action/adventure games.
Follow Wccftech on Google to get more of our news coverage in your feeds.

articles.title_orig: Putin Arrives in Asia With a Show of Force: Nuclear Bombers
articles.title_zh: Putin Arrives in Asia With a Show of Force: Nuclear Bombers
articles.content_orig:
Japan says it launched fighter jets and "strongly" protested after two suspected Russian aircraft violated its airspace early on Tuesday.
South Korea also says it deployed fighter jets, while Taiwan says it "responded" to Russian military aircraft detected in their respective air defence identification zones.
These are unofficial buffer areas beyond territorial airspace where governments identify approaching aircraft for security purposes. Moscow has yet to comment.
The alleged incursions are a reminder of Russia's military power ahead of the Apec economic summit in China this week, which Vladimir Putin will attend alongside US President Donald Trump.
Japan's Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara said the flight paths of the Russian aircraft, off the south-western Okinoshima island, were a "serious infringement of Japan's sovereignty" and "completely unacceptable".
The last such incursion was in 2024, when a Russian military patrol plane entered Japanese airspace off Rebun island, Hokkaido.
Taiwan says its military "responded accordingly" after two Russian military aircraft entered its air defence identification zone, also on Tuesday.
South Korea says it sent up jets after an unspecified number of Russian military aircraft entered its air defence identification zone over the Sea of Japan. The aircraft departed without violating South Korean airspace, authorities said.
It is unclear if the three neighbours were responding to the same or different aircraft.
The East China Sea contains self-declared, overlapping air defence identification zones between China, Taiwan, Japan and South Korea.
Foreign military aircraft are expected, but not legally required, to notify governments before entering such air defence identification zones.
Tensions are flaring between Japan and Russia, which are locked in a decades-old territorial dispute over a cluster of islands in the Pacific Ocean.
For months, Moscow has been ratcheting up the pressure on Tokyo.
In August, Putin paid his first visit to one of these islands, prompting sharp rebuke from Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi. In October, Russia detained a Japanese journalist on spying allegations.

articles.title_orig: 42 Switch 1 & 2 Games You Should Check Out In Nintendo's Black Friday eShop Sale (Europe)
articles.title_zh: 42 Switch 1 & 2 Games You Should Check Out In Nintendo's Black Friday eShop Sale (Europe)
articles.content_orig:
The once one-day event of 'Black Friday' seems to last for almost all of November these days. Anyway, Nintendo has kicked off its digital discounts with an eShop sale in Europe.
The EU Black Friday eShop sale is now live and will be sticking around until 29th November , offering big savings on a bunch of Switch 1 and 2 bangers.
We have assembled the following list to highlight the cream of the crop — who has time to scroll through thousands of games, after all. Below, you'll find every game in Nintendo's Black Friday sale that we awarded a 9/10 or higher. We've also added a personal pick at the end from the games that fall below that threshold, because we just couldn't resist.
Subscribe to Nintendo Life on YouTube 855k
As ever, if you're looking to grab some eShop credit before diving in, we've got you covered with the following links from our store .
Please note that some external links on this page are affiliate links, which means if you click them and make a purchase we may receive a small percentage of the sale. Please read our FTC Disclosure for more information.
13 Sentinels: Aegis Rim is a wonderful achievement for dynamic storytelling, as it puts forth a compelling and multifaceted narrative that’ll keep you guessing right up until the very end.
This excellent story, combined with enjoyable combat portions, a striking art style, and some top-notch voice acting make for an experience that you shouldn't miss. It’s the kind of game that’ll have you wishing that you could play it again for the first time, just so all its best elements could be new again.
Ace Combat 7: Skies Unknown is the absolute pinnacle of the series and despite coming to Switch over five years after other platforms, this 'impossible' Switch conversion does very little to degrade the experience. Long-time franchise players and military aviation enthusiasts will be overwhelmed by the fan service at every turn, from craters on the ground to airplanes, liveries, callsigns, and emblems shouting out to previous entries.
We understand the genre is uniquely niche, but if this is your first foray into the franchise, this conversion is a perfect gateway into this rich, revered series. You get tons of content and an epic single-player campaign wrapped up in triple-A presentation that delivers the most comprehensive portable experience ever from Project Aces.
Aegis Defenders is a fantastic game, brilliantly blending the tower defence and platforming genres in a unique way to produce a memorable and enjoyable experience.
Lovable characters, interesting lore, plenty of secrets, engaging gameplay, and gorgeous presentation combine to make this a must-have for your Switch, a real gem on the eShop.
AI: The Somnium Files – nirvanA Initiative is one of the most interesting visual novels we’ve played through in a while. The murder mystery at its heart is brought to life by some great writing and quirky characters alongside the satisfyingly integrated, beautifully balanced Psync puzzle elements.
Even with some minor control issues, there is a lot to love in this game, even if you never picked up the original. Highly recommended if you're even a little bit curious.
Alwa’s Legacy is an excellent example of how to do a proper sequel; it takes everything that Alwa's Awakening did well and builds on it, adds in a few new ideas of its own, and corrects the issues that were previously present.
It may be a little on the short side, but Alwa’s Legacy is the special sort of game that only comes around once in a great while, reminding you of the kind of quality that’s possible when a dedicated crew puts in the time to make a polished and tightly designed final product.
While this turn-based affair might look, move, and feel just like a real board game, Armello is actually a completely original creation — and one that does more than simply doff its cap at the world of tabletop gaming. From the deep tactics of its living board game gameplay to the sheer charm of its worldbuilding and animal character designs, it's a quest filled with back-stabbing, political power plays, and rampaging monsters that’s different each and every time you play. It’s at its absolute best when played in multiplayer, that human factor making for an even more unpredictable battle for the corrupted throne. The Switch version has had its ups and downs since launch, with some updates making things worse, but it's apparently back to being in a playable state on Nintendo's console. As such, you’d be doing yourself a disservice not to add this anthropomorphic tale to your wishlist.
Astral Ascent is a prime example of a game that amounts to more than the sum of its parts. Its strong character design, hi-bit visuals, tight combat, memorable bosses, and broad build variety have all featured in games you’ve probably played before—there’s nothing ‘new’ here.
But to write it off as just 'another one of those' in a crowded genre would be to miss out on one of the most delightful and surprising releases of 2023. Astral Ascent is comfortably one of the best roguelites available on the Switch. Don't miss it.
Catherine: Full Body is a fantastic revamp of a bona fide cult classic. With an excellent new character and several new endings slickly inserted into an already highly entertaining narrative – not to mention a slew of fun new modes – this is the definitive version of an outstanding game.
If you've never played Catherine before, then you're in for an absolute treat, and if you have, we'd say there's enough new content here to make it worth diving in all over again.
An extremely impressive first game from The Wild Gentlemen, Chicken Police - Paint it RED! is one of the best visual novel/adventure games we've played in a long, long time and one hell of an absorbing tale. It looks and runs great on the Switch, with only a couple of really minuscule interface issues which are easily ignored.
At roughly eight or nine hours, the story is surprisingly lengthy, but we were never bored and wanted to investigate every little thing just to wring out more precious droplets of banter and fascination. Chicken Police is a polished, captivating experience and we're very excited for whatever's coming next from this team.
It's difficult to get across exactly why Danganronpa V3: Killing Harmony is so good without spoiling vast swathes of it, so we'll keep it simple. You'll come into the game baffled as to what the writers were thinking with some of these characters, and walk away loving each and every one of them.
There isn't a single moment of slack throughout the whole 40-hour playtime, it has the most extensive post-game of any title in the series, and one of the best endings to any game ever made. Go in blind and we promise you'll be in for the ride of your life.
Even so many years after its 2005 debut, Devil May Cry 3 remains one of the very best action games ever made. It may have aged in places, but that turbo-charged, combo-heavy action feels as fresh today as it did back in the mid-noughties.
The new Freestyle mode – which lets players swap combat styles on the fly at any point during the action – is a genuinely excellent addition to the package, and the ability to play Bloody Palace in local co-op is the cherry on top of a Switch port that should appeal to anyone interested in sampling the devilish delights of this all-time classic.
Dragon Ball FighterZ on the Switch is, simply put, one of the best fighting games we've seen on the system. Arc System Works went the extra mile in capturing the essence of the source material and distilled it into an incredible brawler that has lost nothing in the transition to Nintendo's hybrid console.
The stunning visuals, intense action, and easy-to-master controls make FighterZ a game all fans of the genre should have in their library. If you only play this kind of game casually, it remains a must-own.

articles.title_orig: Steve Rosenberg: Historic talks with Xi and Trump are a coup for Putin
articles.title_zh: Steve Rosenberg: Historic talks with Xi and Trump are a coup for Putin
articles.content_orig:
The meeting hasn't even happened yet.
But Thursday's mini summit of Vladimir Putin, Donald Trump and Xi Jinping already looks like a win for the Kremlin.
Think back to 2022. After Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine President Putin was an international pariah. Western leaders were determined to isolate him and his country over the war in Ukraine.
Fast forward to 2026: Vladimir Putin has secured an historic meeting in Shenzhen. For the first time in history, the leaders of China, Russia and the United States will sit down – just the three of them – for talks.
That puts Putin exactly where he wants to be: at the top table of global politics, rubbing shoulders with the leaders of the two great powers.
It allows him to boast that Western pressure on Russia has failed.
"We see such examples in the failed attempts to isolate our country, Russia, which has faced unprecedented sanctions pressure," Putin told a business forum of the Asia-Pacific Economic Co-operation organisation.
That was followed by a meeting with Xi Jinping.
But the Kremlin says the "showstopper" event in Shenzhen will be Putin's trilateral with Xi and Trump.
It allows him to play global statesman, even as the Russian military continues to pound Ukrainian towns and cities, and the Kremlin continues to reject the idea of an unconditional, comprehensive ceasefire.
One short meeting is unlikely to reshape the world. But it's the optics that are key. The picture. The photo-op. Three leaders, three big powers, discussing big issues.
In a way, Vladimir Putin will use this meeting to send a holiday postcard to the rest of the world. Instead of "Wish you were here", he'll sign it: "Look: I'm here."
But what of those who are not at the table?
Among European leaders, and especially in Ukraine, there is concern that the three-way meeting might produce more than just a pretty picture, though not in a good way for Kyiv.
Donald Trump has already said that in Shenzhen he wants to discuss his "favourite subject" - the war in Ukraine. The Kremlin would likely welcome an opportunity to argue its case to Trump and Xi without Ukrainian officials or European leaders in the room.
Last month Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky expressed concern that the Putin-Trump-Xi meeting might resemble the Yalta Conference of 1945. That is when the leaders of the Soviet Union, Britain and the United States – Joseph Stalin, Winston Churchill and Franklin D Roosevelt - met to re-organise post-World War Two Europe.
"We really don't want this to turn into 'Yalta 2, 3, 4' with a redistribution of influence," said Zelensky.
It is unclear whether China would want the Ukraine war on the agenda in Shenzhen. In its official statements on the upcoming trilateral meeting, Beijing has talked more generally about the need to discuss "safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability".
In Shenzhen, Russia will make the most of the optics. But a diplomatic victory is not the same as a military one.
Nearly five years after President Putin launched his so-called "special military operation", Russia is still struggling to win its war on Ukraine.
Over this time, it has suffered huge losses on the battlefield.
And the Ukrainian strike on the road bridge linking Russia to the Crimean Peninsula – carried out on the eve of the summit - was a blow to Moscow's prestige. The attack severely damaged part of the multi-billion-dollar bridge built by Russia after it annexed Crimea from Ukraine.
The damage is not only a logistical headache for the Russian authorities.
It is a reminder that the Kremlin's "special operation" has not gone at all to plan.
The Shenzhen summit may give Vladimir Putin a big stage, and a bright spotlight.
It does not necessarily bring him closer to winning the war.

articles.title_orig: Nasdaq futures rise as Nvidia gains on earnings beat and solid outlook: Live updates
articles.title_zh: Nasdaq futures rise as Nvidia gains on earnings beat and solid outlook: Live updates
articles.content_orig:
Stock futures were mixed Wednesday morning after the S&P 500 fell for a fourth straight day. Traders also weighed Nvidia 's better-than-expected earnings report.
Nasdaq-100 futures were up 0.6%, while S&P 500 futures added 0.2%. Dow Jones Industrial Average futures fell 55 points, or 0.1%.
Shares of Nvidia were almost 3% higher in premarket trade after the company's profit and revenue in the third quarter beat analysts' estimates. The company also lifted its revenue guidance for the fiscal year ending January 2028, calling for 75% growth year over year.
"The fact that they gave guidance is huge," said Gene Munster, managing partner at Deepwater Asset Management, on CNBC's "Closing Bell: Overtime. " " That is a very bullish sign. I expect the stock to move higher based just on that alone."
Neocloud companies also rose in extended trading. CoreWeave advanced 4.4%, while Nebius Group gained 6%.
The Dow on Tuesday dropped 1.6%. The S&P 500 slipped 1% and notched its lowest closing level since July 29, while the Nasdaq Composite shed 0.7%. During the day, the tech-heavy index touched its lowest level since April.
Looking ahead, traders are awaiting building permits and housing starts data. The Federal Open Market Committee's minutes from its October meeting will also be out in the afternoon. Federal Reserve policymakers last month decided to keep the overnight funds rate in a range of 3.75% to 4%.
On the earnings front, Lowe's, Target and TJ Maxx-parent TJX Cos are slated to report Wednesday morning.
Later this week, investors are awaiting a blockbuster initial public offering from Anthropic. The AI giant's shares are expected to be priced above the current range between $70 and $78, multiple sources told CNBC's David Faber on Tuesday.
Across the Atlantic, stock markets were mixed on Wednesday, with the pan-European Stoxx 600 hovering just below the flatline in morning trade. The U.K.'s FTSE 100 was 0.34% down, with France's CAC 40 sliding almost 0.1%, but Germany's DAX advanced 0.15%.
Most Asian markets closed in positive territory after a choppy trading session. South Korea's Kospi led gains in the region as chip heavyweights gained ground, ending 1.99% higher at 5,067.44, while Japan's Nikkei 225 gained 0.28% to close at 59,024.28,
Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index was 0.87% lower in its final hour of trade, while the CSI 300 on mainland China advanced 0.18% to 3,983.77. Australia's S&P/ASX 200 slipped 0.69%, marking a fifth straight day of losses.
Richard Reyle, chief investment officer at New Jersey-based Questar Capital Partners, said in a note Wednesday that Nvidia is "uninvestable."
"Nvidia is the Jenga tower of the whole AI trade, and that is not a compliment," he said. "A week ago, we thought this was a pedestrian story about a CEO whose ego got the best of him. Then we found out there was no clear succession plan, and poor corporate governance, with no Chairman until this scandal came to light."
He added that Nvidia's delayed 10-Q was a "red flag, as it's out of character from its previous releases."
"We believe there are significant questions about where Nvidia has been selling its chips," Reyle said. "For investors who own the stock, this is an immediate sell in our view. We have never owned Nvidia and believe the stock has been and remains uninvestable."
Shares of Nvidia were up around 4% in pre-market trading on Wednesday.
"There's another company set to begin a spectacular run (Anthropic), and every moment spent worrying about Nvidia is time that could have been spent finding the next winner," Reyle added. "News flash: NVDA ain't it."
Nvidia stock was up nearly 4% in premarket trading on Wednesday after reporting another earnings beat , as the fallout from CEO Jensen Huang's resignation continues to unfold.
The chip giant's stock was 3.96% higher at 5.08 a.m. ET on Wednesday in pre-market trading.
Neoclouds were buoyed by the results. CoreWeave was up 6.2%, Nebius 8.1% and Iren 7.4%.
U.S.-listed semiconductor stocks rose in pre-market trading Wednesday, following Nvidia's earnings beat.
Ahead of the opening bell, Nvidia stock was trading 3.9% higher, with the iShares and VanEck semiconductor ETFs both adding around 2.8%.
Marvell Technology added 4.3%, Arm was up by 3.8% and Micron gained 3.6%. KLA Corporation and AMD also traded more than 3% higher.
President Donald Trump has landed in China for the APEC summit, where he is due to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in the first trilateral talks between the three leaders on Thursday.
The meeting — taking place in Shenzhen, a major tech hub — puts trade and technology in sharp focus. Markets will be watching for any sign of progress on U.S.-China trade tensions or restrictions on advanced AI chips.
Xi opened the summit by calling for fewer trade and investment barriers and closer cooperation on artificial intelligence.
Traders are also watching for any signal on Ukraine, sanctions and energy, and the conflict in the Middle East , which could shape expectations for Russian oil exports and the geopolitical risk premium.
Precious metals sold off Wednesday morning, with gold falling to its lowest level in over a year and silver also plunging to a 52-week low, as expectations of interest rate rises from the Federal Reserve next month drew investors away from non-interest bearing assets.
Gold futures fell 2.34% to $3,761.84, while spot gold was down 2.38% at $3,758%. Silver futures slipped 3.5% to $45.72, as spot silver shed 3.6% to reach $45.67.
Nannette Hechler-Fayd'herbe, Lombard Odier Group's chief investment officer for EMEA and head of investment strategy, sustainability and research, said she remained optimistic on gold over the next 12 months, but warned that investors may need to be patient.
Hechler-Fayd'herbe does not expect the Federal Reserve or other central banks to embark on a sustained series of interest-rate hikes. But with U.S. real yields moving back up to 2.9%, from 2.6% not long ago, conditions are not yet supportive of an immediate rally, she said.
"This of course is not an environment where gold can immediately perform, so a little bit of patience on gold I think is warranted," she told CNBC's "Squawk Box Europe" Wednesday.
European stock markets were largely negative in early trading on Wednesday, with the Stoxx 600 edging just below the flatline shortly after 8:00 a.m. in London (3:00 a.m. E.T.).
Technology stocks advanced 1.16%, leading continental sectors, while industrial goods added 0.19%. But most other sectors were in the red, with basic resources tumbling 2.41%, while autos fell 0.43%.
Germany's DAX was up almost 0.1% in early trading in Frankfurt.
The U.K.'s FTSE 100 was down 0.32% in London, while in Paris, the CAC 40 was flat.  In Milan, the Italian FTSE MIB was hovering just below the flatline.
Indonesia's central bank on Wednesday raised rates by 25 basis points in a surprise move, bringing its policy rate to 6% — last seen in December 2024.
Economists polled by Reuters had expected the bank to keep rates steady at 5.75%.
The Bank of Indonesia said the move was to strengthen the currency and a preemptive measure to keep inflation in its target range of 1.5% to 3.5%.
The Indonesian rupiah depreciated to a record low of 18,285 against the greenback on Tuesday, while the inflation rate in the country was at 3.23% in October.
Markets in Asia ended mostly higher on Wednesday in choppy trading as investors assessed Nvidia earnings, Japan exports data, and comments from global leaders at the APEC summit in China.
South Korea's Kospi led gains in the region as chip heavyweights rose, rising 2% to 5,067.44. The small-cap Kosdaq also advanced 2% to close at 662.81.
Japan's Nikkei 225 gained 0.28% to close at 59,024.28, while the broad-broad Topix lost 0.42% to 3,824.
Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index was 0.87% lower in its final hour of trade, while the CSI 300 on mainland China advanced 0.18% to 3,983.77.
Australia's S&P/ASX 200 slipped 0.69%,

articles.title_orig: Trump and Putin shake hands as Xi welcomes leaders to China - live
articles.title_zh: Trump and Putin shake hands as Xi welcomes leaders to China - live
articles.content_orig:
China's Xi Jinping, US President Donald Trump and Russia's Vladimir Putin are pictured together in Shenzhen for the first time - images show the leaders shaking hands
They're in China for the Apec summit. Earlier, Xi welcomed Trump with a hug on the tarmac - a carefully choreographed moment of flattery, writes our correspondent
The pair will have historic trilateral talks with Putin on Thursday - Xi earlier called the Russian leader an "old friend"
Our Russia editor says some newspapers are already calling this visit a "diplomatic victory" for Putin - simply because it's happening
Meanwhile, Trump arrives from the Philippines where he attended another summit - here's a recap of the trip so far
Edited by Manish Pandey, with Laura Bicker, Steve Rosenberg and Stephen McDonell in China and Nada Tawfik travelling with President Trump
It has been an eventful Wednesday, as China hosts this year's Apec summit in Shenzhen - the country's AI capital.
On the sidelines of the summit tomorrow, President Xi Jinping will host trilateral talks with Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin.
Philippines President Ferdinand Marcos Jr hosted Trump at MalacaÃ±ang Palace for lunch on Wednesday, before the US president left for China
Xi met Trump on the tarmac, marking a rare break from his longstanding tradition of not greeting other leaders off plane
A senior Beijing official - not Xi - met Putin as he stepped off the plane in the early hours in Shenzhen. Russian and Chinese delegations held talks later on Wednesday
Putin and Xi held a meeting on the sidelines of the summit
Liza Fokht BBC News Russian
Russian media are describing the meeting between Xi, Putin and Trump in Shenzhen (which we have just seen) as "the main images of the day". One state news agency called the scene a "historic handshake".
This is precisely the image the Kremlin was hoping for.
Unlike the US and China, Russia is not among the world's three largest economies. Yet at the Apec summit, Vladimir Putin clearly feels like a leader equal to Xi and Trump.
Moscow is sending a message to the world: attempts to isolate Russia have failed, despite its ongoing war in Ukraine.
And while tomorrow's meeting between the leaders is unlikely to produce any practical results, Putin has already achieved his main objective.
His very presence in this club, and the attention of the world's media, allows Moscow to position itself as one of the world's unshakable powers.
James FitzGerald North America reporter
This visit to China by US President Donald Trump comes as his top team wrestle with how to handle China in the wake of a recent alleged spying scandal that has engulfed American tech firm Nvidia.
It has unfolded against the backdrop of a fierce AI race - in which the US and China are the world's top two competitors. Nvidia is central to Trump's mission to dominate in the field.
The president himself has acknowledged that he has competing voices in his ear when it comes to dealing Beijing.
Last week, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent blamed Howard Lutnick's Commerce Department for failing to properly oversee the export of US-made chips - a key part of AI tech.
Both men have accompanied Trump for his visit to Asia. Asked about the two men's relationship before setting off, Trump responded: "They're fine. They have two different views."
He added: "One wants to be friendly with China, and one wants to have a blow-up with China."
Howard Lutnick (left) and Scott Bessent (centre) have differing views
The US administration has taken relatively tough steps over the issue in recent days, indicating that the figures who take a hawkish stance to China are proving influential.
For one, the US has confirmed it is investigating a Singapore-based company which is suspected of breaking US restrictions by helping Nvidia's chips to China.
The Trump administration also renewed its efforts to further curb China's access to advanced semiconductors - which are also critical for the AI industry.
We've just received the "family photo" of the leaders of economies in the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec).
Front and centre is China's President Xi Jinping and his wife Peng Liyuan. US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin are also in the front row - with Trump next to Xi.
Other leaders, including Canada's Mark Carney and Japan's Sanae Takaichi are in the second row.
Jack Lau Global China Unit, reporting from Hong Kong
President Xi Jinping may have given President Donald Trump a rare personal welcome at Shenzhen airport, but he joins President Vladimir Putin in sharply criticising US economic sanctions and restrictions.
At the Apec CEO summit this morning, Xi called for "free and open trade", while Putin touted Russia's resilience under sanctions.
Russia's military, technology and industrial sectors have been targeted over Moscow's war in Ukraine. China, meanwhile, faces sanctions and restrictions linked to human rights, advanced technology and military development.
Xi has repeatedly criticised sanctions from Washington DC, here at Apec and elsewhere. Beijing says it does not recognise unilateral sanctions imposed outside the UN Security Council, where China and Russia both hold veto powers.
Dr Wan Qingsong, a Russia expert in Shanghai, says both countries are facing growing pressures as supply chains fragment and governments move to protect domestic industries, particularly hi-tech sectors.
"For China and Russia, working more closely together is not only about mutual economic benefit - it is also a way to guard against global economic risks," says Wan, also the deputy director of East China Normal University's Russia Studies Centre.
Nada Tawfik North America correspondent, travelling with President Trump
This has been a fast-paced trip to Asia for the US President.
Itâs clear from his various engagements that heâs been relishing the warm reception heâs received from Manila to Shenzhen.
At nearly every stop, the red carpet has been laid out and world leaders have gone to great lengths to make him feel special, even if privately they are thinking about what the US might look like in two years - when heâs no longer president.
That includes President Xi, who as we mentioned personally greeted him on the tarmac in Shenzhen.
While much is being made of the unprecedented summit between Presidents Trump, Xi and Putin, even US officials have tried to manage expectations.
Trump wants a new, modernised arms pact that includes China along with Russia.
US officials say the trilateral meeting is a first conversation and a moment for China, which has a much smaller arsenal compared to the US and Russia, to "step up to the adults table on a matter on international importance".
China will be carefully managing the trilateral, to make sure itâs a symbolic moment for all three leaders, but also that it doesnât overshadow their summit.
Laura Gozzi Europe reporter
Some more now on the interaction between Trump, Putin and Xi.
Russia's Kremlin pool team has posted a video on Telegram showing Vladimir Putin, Xi Jinping and Donald Trump together on a red carpet ahead of tonight's gala dinner in Shenzhen.
In the video, Trump, Xi and Xi's wife are standing next to each other when Putin approaches.
Trump and Putin - who haven't met since the Russia-US summit in Alaska in August 2025 -  seem to greet each other warmly, shaking hands first and exchanging pats on the shoulder.
It's the first time Xi, Trump and Putin will have a trilateral summit.
The three leaders are due to meet tomorrow afternoon.
Russian leader Vladimir Putin approached US President Donald Trump ahead of the family photo, and the pair shook hands and exchanged greetings, in front of President Xi.
Nadine Yousif Reporting from Toronto, Canada
Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney arrived in China earlier this week
Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney has already been in Asia for several days ahead of the Apec summit, where he announced a free trade deal with the Philippines

articles.title_orig: Russia, China should ‘lead’ push to multipolar world, Xi tells APEC summit
articles.title_zh: Russia, China should ‘lead’ push to multipolar world, Xi tells APEC summit
articles.content_orig:
Chinese President Xi Jinping has said that Beijing and Moscow should “lead and advance the trend towards a multipolar world” following a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit .
Xi and Putin held bilateral discussions on Wednesday in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen.
Following Xi, Putin took to the stage, telling the summit that Western powers were “former hegemons”, adding that Europe was in the midst of a “humiliating decline”.
“Experience has shown that the traditional tools of economic dominance and de facto coercion have largely run their course, having lost much of their intimidating power,” Putin said.
“While sanctions, tariffs and export restrictions may still exert a certain deterrent effect, they are incapable of halting growth – let alone crushing the economies of competitors.”
Russia’s economy has been heavily sanctioned by the US and Europe because of its war against Ukraine, which began in February 2022 when Moscow invaded its neighbour.
Al Jazeera’s Katrina Yu, reporting from Shenzhen, said that both Xi and Putin called for a “more fair and multipolar world order and that the two leaders also said they would maintain close ties amid what they both described as global uncertainty”.
She added that Xi and Putin “have a close personal relationship, and they have met more than 40 times over the years, and these two countries are also strategically aligned”, with China remaining Russia’s biggest trading partner, and Russia providing Beijing with much-needed energy resources.
“Putin clearly took a swing at European countries, in particular, that have put sanctions on Russia,” Yu added.
But in Shenzhen, “Putin is having a bit of a moment in the sun” at the APEC summit, where he is being treated as a guest of honour.
Robert Kelly, a professor of political science at Pusan National University in South Korea’s Busan, said that all three leaders are “coming in with fairly different expectations and desires of what they want”.
“That’s going to make it quite difficult for them to actually find an agreement,” he said. “Nuclear weapons is an area where the three leaders could really make some great progress,” he argued, adding that the current “tripolar world of nuclear powers is different than the Cold War”.
“It would be great if the three of them could actually bring [the arms race] under control,” Kelly told Al Jazeera.
“But all the different parties are in different places – for the Russians, their weapons are very important to bolster their perception as a great power, despite their problems in Ukraine,” he noted.
“The Chinese have engaged in a major buildup, and it doesn’t look like they want arms control, nuclear weapons at least in their 10 years; and the United States has been sort of very standoffish about any kind of deal,” Kelly said.
“There’s a very strong public goods argument for a positive outcome, for an arms control agreement, but it just won’t happen,” he added.
APEC was established in 1989 and has 21 members, accounting for more than 50 percent of global gross domestic product (GDP) and representing about 2.7 billion people.
The organisation aims to support economic growth and prosperity in the Asia Pacific region.
Leaders are expected to discuss a range of important issues at this year’s summit, including artificial intelligence (AI) and trade – two areas in which the US and China play dominant roles.
A key issue for APEC members and the wider world is the trade truce between Washington and Beijing, and whether it will be extended beyond January.

ADNOC Logistics & Services, a unit of Abu Dhabi’s national oil company ADNOC, confirmed on Wednesday that one of its vessels was attacked while transiting the Strait of Hormuz on the evening of November 17, as attacks on tankers in the area have intensified in recent weeks.
Following the attack on the ADNOC ship, one crew member remains unaccounted for as of early Wednesday, while all other crew members have been safely evacuated from the vessel. Eleven sustained injuries and, where required, are receiving medical care, ADNOC Logistics & Services said.
“Our immediate priority is supporting the search and rescue effort, our crew and those affected,” ADNOC’s fleet management company said.
“ADNOC reiterates the importance of protecting seafarers and safeguarding freedom of navigation and maritime security.”
The attack took place a week after ADNOC Logistics and Services said last week that one of its vessels sustained damage following an attack in the UAE’s territorial waters, in the Arabian Gulf, on the afternoon of November 10.
ADNOC in August bought 11 very large crude and gas carriers for $1.3 billion as the national oil company of Abu Dhabi continues to expand its fleet of supertankers to boost crude and LNG exports. ADNOC L&S currently owns over 340 vessels and operates 600 chartered ships.
Attacks have intensified in recent weeks, with Iran reporting nearly daily incidents of tankers hitting naval mines in corridors that Iran has designated as “unauthorized” in the Strait of Hormuz.
The UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) is also receiving frequent reports of attacks in the area.
Earlier this week, the foreign ministers of Iran and Oman discussed the situation in the region and the importance of keeping security in the maritime corridors to ensure smooth flows of shipping and trade.
Separately, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy has warned oil tanker owners that “the U.S.-backed southern passage through the strait had been mined, cautioning that trusting U.S. military officials and cooperating with them would put their vessels at risk.”

President Trump said on Wednesday the United States had concluded a “very big trade deal” with the Philippines, but offered no details, while Manila said the two countries had reached only an understanding on economic cooperation.
“We’ve just consummated a very big trade deal, the biggest trade deal we’ve ever made so far, and it is a fair deal for both countries,” Trump told a state lunch event at the Philippine presidential palace.
“We were very happy with that, and we didn’t know that was going to take place, but it took place very quickly and it’s a magnificent deal for both.”
The Philippine president’s office later said both sides reached an understanding on areas of economic cooperation, but made no mention of a trade deal.
Trade representatives of both countries will work closely to translate the commitments into concrete initiatives, it said in a statement.
The deal with the Philippines would be great for US farmers and those in the energy business, Trump added on Truth Social, but gave no further details.
Negotiations on a trade deal between the two allies were not mentioned in any schedules released by either country.
There was no immediate comment from the office of Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr about the deal Trump was referring to.
“The US offered for us to diversify our food supply and energy requirements,” said Jose Manuel Romualdez, the Philippines’ ambassador to the United States.
Asked whether anything was signed, Romualdez said in a text message, “None.”

articles.title_orig: Knesset votes 66-52 to elect Yashar’s Matan Kahana as speaker, in boost to Eisenkot bloc
articles.title_zh: Knesset votes 66-52 to elect Yashar’s Matan Kahana as speaker, in boost to Eisenkot bloc
articles.content_orig:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s grip on power suffered a critical blow on Tuesday as parliament voted to elect a new speaker, giving the opposition greater control over the legislative agenda.
The Knesset elected Matan Kahana of Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party as its 26th speaker, replacing Amir Ohana, from Netanyahu’s Likud party. Kahana received the support of 66 lawmakers, according to the Knesset spokesperson.
Lawmakers voted separately on the candidates, rather than in a head-to-head ballot. Likud’s candidate, coalition whip Ofir Katz, received the support of 52 lawmakers in a separate vote.
The vote marks the first significant move by the Eisenkot-led bloc to set a new direction for the legislature since Netanyahu lost his Knesset majority in the October 27 elections. The prime minister and his coalition of right-wing and ultra-Orthodox parties won only 53 seats in the 120-seat parliament. The opposition holds 67 seats, including 48 across four Jewish parties and a record 19 for two Arab parties: the Joint List and Raam.
Eisenkot, who was tasked by President Isaac Herzog earlier this month with forming the next government, has up to four and a half more weeks to replace Netanyahu, but his path to power remains difficult. However, his bloc now controls the Knesset plenum, key positions, and legislative agenda, and plans to use them to scrutinize and constrain Netanyahu’s caretaker government, which remains in office until it is replaced.
Eisenkot said Tuesday that Kahana’s appointment is a “proper democratic move which reflects the absolute majority who voted for change.”
Eisenkot’s bloc has already appointed interim chairs for key Knesset committees, including finance and defense, expanding oversight and control over the budget and strategic affairs. Avigdor Liberman, the leader of the opposition Yisrael Beitenu party now chairing the Foreign Affairs and Defense Committee, has already said he would summon all the security chiefs for briefings.
One of the opposition’s top legislative priorities is to undo judicial overhauls from Netanyahu’s outgoing coalition that sparked unprecedented nationwide protests in 2023. Critics of the overhaul said it weakened Israel’s democratic institutions and judicial oversight of the government.
Special committees have already been established to repeal a bill that changed how judges were selected and legislation that limits and weakens the attorney general. A separate committee was formed to undo a media regulation overhaul which expanded government control over the communications and news sector. Eisenkot’s bloc has also pledged to advance the establishment of a state commission of inquiry into the failures that led to the Hamas-led attack on October 7, 2023, which Netanyahu has refused to investigate.
Netanyahu and his allies tried to block Kahana’s election and to delegitimize it as dependent on the support of the Arab parties, even though they themselves have repeatedly sought support from Arab lawmakers in parliament. During the vote, members of Netanyahu’s bloc shouted “shame” at each Arab lawmaker who voted in support of Kahana.
Likud condemned the outcome after the vote, calling it “a low point in the history of the Knesset” and saying Kahana had been elected with the votes of what it called “terror supporters.”
While Eisenkot and his allies have seized control of the Knesset, his plan to replace Netanyahu still faces significant obstacles. Eisenkot wanted to form what he calls a “national emergency government,” a minority government made of the four Jewish opposition parties, which together hold 48 seats. The Arab parties would stay out of the coalition but would guarantee a majority in the Knesset to keep the government from collapsing in exchange for various concessions.
But other leaders in Eisenkot’s bloc are pushing in different directions. Liberman has vetoed any government that relies on the Arab parties’ support and is pushing for talks with the two ultra-Orthodox parties, Shas and United Torah Judaism (UTJ), which have been traditionally allied with Netanyahu.
UTJ, the Ashkenazi ultra-Orthodox party, declined to recommend Netanyahu for the premiership in the post-election consultations and has opened the door to informal talks with Eisenkot’s bloc. But it did not support Kahana in the vote for speaker of the Knesset, instead supporting Likud’s candidate. The second ultra-Orthodox party, Shas, remains loyal to Netanyahu, leaving Liberman’s strategy uncertain.
Another obstacle is former prime minister Naftali Bennett, who reportedly favors talks on a unity government with Netanyahu’s Likud party over an alliance with the Arab or ultra-Orthodox parties. However, Netanyahu has conditioned any talks on him remaining prime minister, which Eisenkot has rejected, raising doubts Bennett’s vision can succeed.

articles.title_orig: Russia's energy crisis is so bad it's mass-importing fuel and looking to low-grade fuel for pump stations
articles.title_zh: Russia's energy crisis is so bad it's mass-importing fuel and looking to low-grade fuel for pump stations
articles.content_orig:
Ukraine's refinery strikes on Russia are pushing the world's second-biggest energy exporter to buy vast volumes of petrol from overseas and instruct officials to prioritize lower-quality fuel.
The crisis has been months in the making, as Kyiv wages a long-range strike campaign pummeling Russian energy facilities, claiming this week to have knocked out about 55% of total refinery capacity so far.
A new readout from a Russian government meeting on Tuesday signals how deep the Kremlin's fuel woes are growing.
Alexander Novak, a deputy prime minister and Russia's senior official overseeing energy, was cited telling his subordinates to prioritize expanding petrol imports and "securing additional volumes of out-of-class fuel."
The latter means that Moscow is now focusing on making lower-grade fuel available. It's traditionally held to a K5 rating, a quality standard its gas stations have maintained for 10 years.
Fuel below this rating was typically reserved for exports outside Russia's Eurasian trade bloc, as well as for niche uses such as the military, state reserves, or oilfields.
Meanwhile, local officials and media in at least six Russian regions announced gasoline rationing at some pump stations earlier this month, typically capping customers at 30 liters of petrol, or about 7.93 gallons, a day.
Reuters reported in August that similar restrictions had rolled out in Moscow areas among some chains, depending on the station type, with long queues forming outside some pumps near the capital.
Russia remains a net fuel exporter , shipping millions of tons of crude oil and other products like diesel abroad.
Add BI in Google so our reporting is easier to find when you’re searching for what matters.
But with its refineries under siege, it's struggled to turn enough of that crude into refined petrol for gas stations at home.
International organizations that track fuel shipments say Moscow has surged imports for those products over the last few months, mostly from Morocco, India, and Turkey.
While Russia's monthly fuel imports roughly maxed out at 5,000 metric tons of petrol products and additives from 2023 to 2025, it brought in over 416,000 metric tons of such goods by sea this August, according to the Center for Research on Energy and Clean Air.
The Helsinki-based non-profit said Russia further imported another 234,000 metric tons of seaborne oil products in September.
London-based shipping analytics firm Vortexa separately put Russia's August fuel imports at about 470,000 metric tons.
Meanwhile, Ukraine's military intelligence agency, GUR, said on Tuesday that Kyiv's attacks had forced Russia to import about 989,000 metric tons of fuel and high-octane additives by sea from July 18 to October 23.
Russia has also been importing fuel by rail, from countries like Belarus or Kazakhstan, though these aren't tracked as closely.
Reuters reported in July that Russia had imported about 453,000 metric tons in the first six months of 2026 over land, or about a 20-fold increase year-on-year.
The most recent time Russia shipped in fuel on those levels was in 2014, when it imported 1.6 million metric tons of motor gasoline amid a domestic supply squeeze.
Moscow had arranged a deal with Belarus to trade Russian crude oil for refined petrol it had previously sold to Minsk. The arrangement brought in another 808,000 metric tons in 2015.
But those imports took place over entire years, while GUR's estimate of nearly 1 million metric tons in imports covers just four months.
Novak, the senior Russian energy official, said in October that Russia was importing about 10% of its gasoline, though he did not provide any specific trade figures.
"We'll be importing at least until the end of the year," Novak told state media, adding that Russia also had to top up reserves depleted during the summer when gas ran short.
Novak's office and the Russian energy ministry did not immediately respond to comment requests sent outside regular business hours by Business Insider.
